I've written the network for `health_gathering` by hand, with no training and no game. My guess is an average score of about **900 (plausible range 350–1800)**, with low confidence. It has only been tested on synthetic frames I built myself, because the real game can't run here.

**How it plays:** the floor is green and medkits aren't, so the network looks for small non-green spots on the floor and steers toward them. When it sees none, it walks forward. When a wall gets close, it turns toward the side with more open floor, and it never presses straight into a wall.

- **Medkit detectors (layer 1 → layer 2):** 48 detectors cover four bands of floor rows, from far (rows 15–16) to near (rows 25–27). Each one compares a centre patch with the patches on its left and right and fires only when the centre is less green than both. That rules out wall edges, which a first version wrongly read as medkits when walking alongside a wall.
- **Wall detectors:** measure how much green floor is visible a short way ahead and very close ahead, plus how open the left and right sides are.
- **Output:** each detector votes for one of the five actions depending on where on screen it fires, and nearer medkits get bigger votes. If nothing fires, forward wins by a small default; when a wall is very close, forward is blocked.
- **Weapon sprite:** the lower bands skip the centre columns, in case a gun is drawn at the bottom of the screen.

**Synthetic results:** I built a simple fake room (green floor, plain walls, white medkits with a red cross) and tried random positions under four colour and lighting variants:
- With no medkit in view, none of 240 frames made it veer toward a phantom medkit.
- With one medkit in view, it steered the right way about 80–90% of the time. Most misses were medkits very close or right on the line between two steering zones.
- Walls ahead, corners and walls alongside all made it turn away as intended.

**Main risks**, all because I don't know the real colours or s
